verdict.rationale: Microsoft Graph exposes a substantial, well-documented, machine-readable API (channels, messages, teams/channel creation, exports, webhooks, agents toolkit CLI) covering many UI actions, and the CLI mirrors IDE extension features, showing real API-parity intent. But community evidence notes API integration is heavyweight (full Azure/Graph stack vs simple webhooks), some UI actions (e.g., muting, threading UX, reactions) lack clear API parity evidence, and there's no single unified API surface matching 100% of UI capabilities like meetings/calling nuances.
